rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a foundational multimodal configuration to establish baseline performance. This configuration tests key design choices (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA+ViT encoders, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) that are critical for understanding the impact of modality, profile, and fusion strategies. It isolates the effect of combining RNA and image modalities with advanced aggregation/fusion methods, providing early insights into which components matter most.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves moderate performance. This experiment tests changing the image encoder to resnet50 and aggregation to avgpool while keeping fusion as weighted, isolating the impact of these components. It balances exploration (testing alternative image encoders and aggregation methods) and exploitation (focusing on key design choices from the baseline).

Existing evidence shows config_007 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation could further enhance results, balancing exploitation of current high performers with exploration of key design choices.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) has the highest accuracy. This experiment tests changing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while keeping other parameters identical. It isolates the RNA encoder's impact, a critical design choice, to determine if this component significantly affects performance. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a key variable.

Existing evidence shows that config_009 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method fixed) improves performance. This isolates the effect of aggregation, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of config_009. It balances exploitation of a high-performing baseline with exploration of a key hyperparameter.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_019) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping transformer aggregation, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It clarifies whether the fusion method is critical for performance, balancing exploitation of high-performing components with exploration of design choices.

Existing evidence shows that config_019 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the strong foundation of config_019's successful configuration.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger visual model) further improves performance, isolating the effect of image representation. It builds on the current top-performing configuration while exploring a critical design choice with high potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_032) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from transformer to avgpool (while keeping other key components like scvi_n200 and ViT) affects performance, isolating the impact of aggregation. This clarifies if transformer aggregation is critical for high performance, balancing exploration of aggregation choices with exploitation of the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_032). This experiment tests the effect of fusion type (weighted vs. concat) while keeping other parameters constant. It isolates the impact of fusion strategy, which is critical for multimodal performance, and builds on the promising combination of scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation.
